## Overview

|             |                                                 |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| **Input**   | `autism_ipp_recoded.rds`                        |
| **Output**  | `autism_ipp_imputed.rds`                        |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Dependencies"}
The parent folder of this document's folder should contain a folder called `Data` with the file `autism_ipp_recoded.rds`. The script `autism_ipp_recodes.qmd` will produce this file if it is not yet present.
:::

## Set up

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Working directory"}
Quarto runs code from the folder this `.qmd` file is saved in, so you don't need `setwd()`. Relative paths like `../Data/` work as long as the folder layout above is in place.
:::

### Load packages

```{r}
#| label: load-packages

library(tidyverse)
#install.packages("mice") # run once then comment out
library(mice)
```

### Load original data

```{r}
#| label: load-data

original_data <- readRDS("../Data/autism_ipp_recoded.rds")
```

## Set up imputation

### Select variables

First, select the variables that you want to include in the imputation model. These should include all of the variables that will be in your analysis (in the form they will be in for the analysis) as well as any variables that you think may help predict/fill in missing values. The data object should only include these columns.

```{r}
#| label: set-up-imputation-variables

set.seed(20261022) # ensure reproducibility

imputation_vars <- c(
  # Participant characteristics
  "gender", "race", "degree",
  "masters_nasp", "specialist_nasp", "doctorate_nasp", "doctorate_apa",
  "intern_school", "intern_hospital", "intern_detention", "intern_health_sci",
  "intern_residential", "intern_community_mh", "intern_consortium", "intern_other",
  "practice_setting", "district",

  # Independent variables
  "perceived_know", "fact_know_asksp", "train_quality",
  "att_effic_atihct", "att_quality_atihct",

  # Dependent variables
  "interpro_num", "interpro_freq", "interag_num", "interag_freq"
)

data_to_impute <- original_data[imputation_vars]

# Grab names of variables that have no missing values
missing_n <- colSums(is.na(data_to_impute))
print(missing_n)
no_miss <- names(missing_n[missing_n == 0])

# Identify dependent variables
dependent_vars <- c("interpro_num", "interpro_freq", "interag_num", "interag_freq")
not_dv_vars <- setdiff(imputation_vars, dependent_vars)
```

There is no missingness in gender, race, degree, intern location, practice setting, or fact_know_asksp. These can still be used to impute other variables, but they do not need to be imputed themselves. We also will not impute our dependent variables, both on principle, and because we do not know whether missing values in this case are actually missing or indicate 0 collaboration.

### Set imputation methods

```{r}
#| label: set-up-imputation-methods

# First mark every NA as eligible for imputation
where <- is.na(data_to_impute)

# Initialize in order to edit methods
initial <- mice(data_to_impute, maxit = 0, printFlag = FALSE)
method <- initial$method
predictor_matrix <- initial$predictorMatrix

# Remove imputation for dependent vars
method[dependent_vars] <- ""
predictor_matrix[dependent_vars, ] <- 0
where[, dependent_vars] <- F

# Remove imputation for variables without missingness
method[no_miss] <- ""
predictor_matrix[no_miss, ] <- 0

# Double check that the methods look correct
print(method) # pmm works well for continuous, polyreg works for unordered categorical
```

### Deal with problematic variables

There are many very sparse categories of gender, which cause gender to be dropped as a predictor in the imputation models. As such, remove gender as a predictor in the imputation model. Additionally, there are structural NAs in the credential variables, so these NAs will also not be imputed, the variables will not be predictors, and constant degree will not be used to impute.

```{r}
#| label: remove-variables

# Gender
predictor_matrix[, "gender"] <- 0

# Accreditation
credential_vars <- c("masters_nasp",
                     "specialist_nasp",
                     "doctorate_nasp",
                     "doctorate_apa")
degree_group <- as.character(data_to_impute$degree)

# Accreditation NAs for nonmatching degree groups are structural NAs, so do not impute
where[which(degree_group != "Master's" | is.na(degree_group)), "masters_nasp"] <- F # for masters_nasp where degree is not master's or degree is missing, do not impute
where[which(degree_group != "Specialist" | is.na(degree_group)), "specialist_nasp"] <- F
where[which(degree_group != "Doctorate" | is.na(degree_group)), "doctorate_nasp"] <- F
where[which(degree_group != "Doctorate" | is.na(degree_group)), "doctorate_apa"] <- F

# Don't use the accreditation variables as predictors for other variables
predictor_matrix[, credential_vars] <- 0

# Degree is constant within each accreditation variable's applicable group,
# so don't use it to impute those accreditation variables
predictor_matrix[credential_vars, "degree"] <- 0
```

## Run imputation

Now, we will run the imputation model with the predictor matrix and methods that we set above.

```{r}
#| label: run-imputation

imputed_data <- mice(data_to_impute,
                     m = 20,
                     maxit = 20,
                     method = method,
                     predictorMatrix = predictor_matrix,
                     where = where,
                     seed = 20261022, # same seed for reproducibility
                     printFlag = FALSE)
```

## Check imputation

To check that the imputation model ran correctly, we check that the only remaining NAs are for respondents who had NAs in the dependent variable(s). These individuals will be dropped from the analysis.

```{r}
#| label: check-imputation
#| message: true

completed_datasets <- complete(imputed_data, action = "all")
check_results <- data.frame()

# Check each imputed dataset
for (imputation_number in seq_along(completed_datasets)) { # loop across datasets
  current_data <- completed_datasets[[imputation_number]]

  # rows where at least one dependent variable is missing
  row_has_missing_dependent <- rowSums(is.na(current_data[dependent_vars])) > 0

  for (variable in not_dv_vars) { # loop across non-DV vars

    # NAs that occur in rows where no dependent variable is missing (& not structural)
    na_count <- sum(is.na(current_data[[variable]]) & where[, variable] & !row_has_missing_dependent)

    # Save the result for this variable and imputation
    check_results <- rbind(check_results, data.frame(imputation = imputation_number,
                                                     variable = variable,
                                                     unexpected_na_count = na_count))
  }
}

# Keep only problems, unexpected NAs with a count above zero
problems <- subset(check_results, unexpected_na_count > 0)
if (nrow(problems) == 0) {
  message("PASS: all remaining NAs are in rows where a dependent variable is missing.")
} else {
  print(problems)
  stop("Check failed: some NAs are in rows where all dependent variables have values.")
}
```

## Save data

```{r}
saveRDS(imputed_data, "../Data/autism_ipp_imputed.rds")
```
